title: Access the generic call and user frame from within a method — S7_generic_call
code: # S7_generic_call() reports the call to the generic: foo := new_generic("x") method(foo, class_double) <- function(x) {   list(nearest = S7_generic_call(), user = S7_generic_call(skip = "super")) } foo(1) #> $nearest #> foo(1) #>  #> $user #> foo(1) #>   # Set skip = "super" to skip past super() re-dispatches: Number := new_class(parent = class_double) method(foo, Number) <- function(x) {   foo(super(x, class_double)) } foo(Number(1)) #> $nearest #> foo(super(x, class_double)) #>  #> $user #> foo(Number(1)) #>   # S7_user_frame() supplies the enclosing environment for non-standard # evaluation, so an expression can mix columns of the data with variables # from where the generic was called, like subset(): keep_rows := new_generic("data") method(keep_rows, class_data.frame) <- function(data, condition) {   rows <- eval(substitute(condition), data, S7_user_frame())   data[rows, , drop = FALSE] }  threshold <- 4 df <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = c(2, 5, 8)) # `x` and `y` come from the data frame; `threshold` from this frame keep_rows(df, x + y > threshold) #>   x y #> 2 2 5 #> 3 3 8  # S7_generic_fun() returns the generic itself, e.g. to use its name in a # message: bar := new_generic("x") method(bar, class_double) <- function(x) {   generic <- S7_generic_fun()   paste0("Called ", generic@name, "()") } bar(1) #> [1] "Called bar()"
